ex_vivo_detail: Ex vivo lipolysis assays in human plasma: apoC-II-deficient human plasma (TG = 1711 mg/dL), pooled human hypertriglyceridemic plasma (TG = 300-600 mg/dL) and individual patient HTG plasma (TG 331-1669 mg/dL), each incubated with LPL plus peptide. Also human VLDL and HDL isolated from plasma and incubated with D6PV to test apoC-III displacement, and fluorescent D6PV incubated with pooled human HTG plasma and separated by FPLC. Mouse plasma from C57Bl/6 and hAPOC3-Tg mice was also treated ex vivo with LPL and D6PV (Fig. 7B).
in_vitro_detail: Cell-free/biophysical assays: circular dichroism spectroscopy, DMPC vesicle clearance assay, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of peptide-lipid trilayers, and ABCA1-mediated cholesterol efflux assays.

concentration_time_figure.locator: Fig. 8B (mice, SC) and Fig. 8C (nonhuman primates, SC); fig. S11 (IV) referenced but not reproduced in this text
concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: (B) PK results of C57Bl/6 mice injected subcutaneously with a single dose of D6PV at 1, 10, and 100 mg/kg.
concentration_time_figure.note: Fig. 8B and 8C are described in the body as PK results after single SC doses; the accompanying text reports Cmax, Tmax and bioavailability from these panels. fig. S11 is cited for the IV half-life data but is a supplementary figure not included in this file.

bioanalytical_method: Liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) after protein precipitation of EDTA-plasma with 3:1 acetonitrile:methanol, using Delta6PL as internal standard; lower limit of quantitation 0.2 μg/mL, calibration linear from 0.2 to 40 μg/mL. PK parameters fitted by a multi-compartmental model in WinNonLin.
bioanalytical_quote: Peptide concentrations in plasma were measured by liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). ... The lower limit of quantitation was 0.2 μg/mL.
notes: Two half-lives are reported for D6PV in mice after IV dosing: a 3 h initial-phase and a 9 h terminal-phase value. Both are described by the authors as elimination half-lives ('the elimination half-life for the initial phase (t1/2,α)' and 'the elimination half-life for the terminal phase (t1/2,z)'), so neither is an absorption half-life; the headline half_life is the terminal 9 h value and both are recorded in half_life_elimination. The 42-50 h terminal half-life is a NONHUMAN PRIMATE value, not a mouse value, and is kept in a separate agent object. Bioavailability after SC dosing was over 65% at 1 and 10 mg/kg in mice and approximately 80% in nonhuman primates; no absorption half-life was fitted. AUC is described only qualitatively ('A nonlinear increase in the area-under-the-curve (AUC) was observed between the 10 and 100 mg/kg dose groups'), with no numeric values or units, so auc is 'not reported'. Other reported mouse PK parameters: steady-state volume of distribution Vss 81 mL/kg and clearance ~8 mL/kg/h. The allometrically scaled human terminal half-life of 3-4 days is a projection, not a measurement, and is deliberately not recorded as a half-life. Methods state the mouse PK study had '4 groups, 3 doses ... and 2 dose routes ... with 18 animals in each group' for 72 mice, which is internally inconsistent (3 x 2 = 6 arms); recorded verbatim.
